Breed a pair of matrices into a clutch

Source: R/breed.R
breed.Rd

Combines two matrices into a clutch: aligns them on overlapping row / column names when both carry dimnames, computes a compact set of comparison statistics (Pearson and Spearman correlations, RMSE, MAE, NA counts, value ranges), and stores the aligned matrices alongside a tidy long form. The result is the canonical BiHeat input — pass it to incubate() to set rendering options and then to plot() to draw, or straight to plot() (or biheat()) for defaults.

Usage

breed(
  a,
  b,
  upper_name = NULL,
  lower_name = NULL,
  align = c("intersect", "by_position")
)

Arguments

a, b

Matrices (or objects coercible via as.matrix()). a is drawn in the upper triangle, b in the lower triangle.

upper_name, lower_name

Optional labels. When NULL, BiHeat reads the symbol names you passed in via substitute(), so breed(observed, predicted) records "observed" and "predicted" automatically.

align

"intersect" (default) or "by_position".

Value

A clutch: a list with upper, lower, data, meta, align, align_report, upper_name, lower_name, config.

Details

Alignment rules (align = "intersect", the default):

  • Both matrices carry rownames and colnames: take the intersection on each side. The clutch remembers which rows / columns were dropped.

  • Only one side carries names on a given axis, or neither does: that axis is aligned by position, which requires identical length.

  • No overlap on a named axis: error.

Pass align = "by_position" to skip the name-based logic entirely and require identical shape.

See also

incubate(), biheat()

Examples

set.seed(1)
species <- LETTERS[1:6]
sites   <- letters[1:5]
observed  <- matrix(runif(30), 6, 5, dimnames = list(species, sites))
predicted <- observed + matrix(rnorm(30, sd = 0.1), 6, 5,
                               dimnames = list(species, sites))

clutch <- breed(observed, predicted)
clutch
plot(clutch)
